title: LLM Fallback & Regional Routing — Hands-on Reference Implementation
content:
Purpose:
This hands-on reference doc is intended for Solutions Engineering workshops where the ask is: show a reproducible POC that demonstrates regional routing, model-fallback policies, and an observable rollout for an LLM-backed chat feature using Redwood Inference (hosted + dedicated variants).

Scope and learning goals:
- Provision a minimal test app that calls Redwood API and can switch between model variants and regions.
- Implement a smart-routing policy: prefer low-latency region, fall back to a cheaper quantized variant if capacity is constrained, and an ultimate fallback to a small hosted model to preserve availability.
- Wire telemetry so attendees can see latency, model selection, and cost estimates in the Console.
- Show a simple canary rollout and safety rollback on quality-regression detection.

Target audience:
- Customer engineers, platform eng teams, and product owners evaluating Redwood for production inference.

Prereqs (local & account):
- Redwood account with API key + permission to create routes and model variants.
- Optional: Dedicated pool provisioned (or use sandbox dedicated from Solutions infra).
- Local environment: Node 18+ or Python 3.10+, curl, kubectl (if deploying example to k8s), Docker (optional).

Workshop flow (90–120 minutes):
1) 10m: Overview & architecture diagram (present)
2) 15m: Quick environment setup (attendees run bootstrap script)
3) 35m: Hands-on labs — implement routing & fallback policy, deploy sample app to a single k8s namespace or run locally
4) 20m: Observability — inspect traces, cost per-route, latency distribution, and trigger a canary rollout
5) 10–30m: Q&A and optional extension (private on-prem demo)

Reference architecture (brief):
- App layer: simple chat service (Node or Python) that forwards user messages to Redwood via an API route.
- Redwood routing layer: Route config with priority: regional-match -> dedicated-pool-variant -> quantized-variant -> hosted-small-fallback.
- Observability: Redwood Console dashboards + app-side traces instrumented with OpenTelemetry.

Quick bootstrap (Linux/macOS)
1) Clone example repo:
   git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples.git && cd examples/llm-routing-workshop

2) Create .env with API key and local config (example):
   REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-test-xxxx
   REDWOOD_DEFAULT_ROUTE=workshop-regional-route
   REGION_PREFERENCE=us-west1,us-central1,us-east1

3) Install deps (Node):
   npm install

Mini app (behavior summary):
- POST /chat -> forwards to Redwood route; records which model variant responded; emits metric via stdout in JSON for workshop demo.

Example request payload (pseudo):
{
  "input": "Summarize the following conversation…",
  "conversation": [...],
  "user_id": "acct-123"
}

Routing policy example (YAML style) — create as route config via Console or API
---
route_name: workshop-regional-route
priority_rules:
  - name: local-latency-preference
    match: request.region in ["us-west1", "us-central1"]
    action:
      prefer: ["models/redwood-dedicated/v1", "models/redwood-quantized/v1"]
  - name: cost-safe-fallback
    match: default
    action:
      fallback_chain: ["models/redwood-quantized/v1", "models/redwood-hosted-small/v1"]
health_checks:
  - probe: latency
    threshold_ms: 1200
    on_fail: skip_variant

Notes on policy: this structure is a conceptual mapping — actual API uses route creation endpoints (see linked_artifacts PR). For the workshop we use the Console to apply an equivalent policy so attendees can visualize the precedence tree.

Sample Python snippet (using requests) to hit Redwood route and surface variant metadata:
```python
import os
import requests

API_KEY = os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')
ROUTE = os.getenv('REDWOOD_DEFAULT_ROUTE')

def chat(prompt, user_id="demo-user"):
    url = f"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routes/{ROUTE}/generate"
    headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
    payload = {"input": prompt, "metadata": {"user_id": user_id}}
    r = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers, timeout=15)
    r.raise_for_status()
    data = r.json()
    # Redwood returns model_variant and routing.reason for visibility
    print("model_variant:", data.get("model_variant"))
    print("routing_reason:", data.get("routing_reason"))
    return data.get("output")
```

K8s quick deploy (optional)
- We provide a lightweight deployment manifest that runs the Node app in a single namespace workshop-llm. It uses a simple Liveness probe and exposes port 8080. Adjust env var REDWOOD_API_KEY via k8s secret.
- Useful commands during workshop:
   kubectl -n workshop-llm logs -f deploy/llm-demo
   kubectl -n workshop-llm port-forward svc/llm-demo 8080:8080

Observability checklist (what attendees should verify)
- In Console: per-route latency histogram shows increased p50 when dedicated pool is starved
- Route-level cost estimate chart updates when fallback to quantized variant occurs
- Request trace shows model_variant tag and fallback hop list
- App logs show variant metadata printed for each request (from sample snippet)

Canary rollout pattern (manual for workshop)
1) Create two variants: models/redwood-dedicated/v1 (current) and models/redwood-dedicated/v2-canary (new weights or prompt tuning).
2) Route config: weight 90:10 (v1:v2) for 1 hour. Monitor quality metrics (accuracy on prompt set) and token-level cost.
3) If quality regression > 3% on tracked prompts, rollback to 100% v1. The Console alerting can trigger a webhook; we show how to patch the route via API to set weights back.

Troubleshooting common issues
- 401 from API: ensure REDWOOD_API_KEY is set and not expired; check team permissions to modify routes.
- Unexpected fallback to hosted-small: check dedicated pool capacity and health probes in Console; also ensure route match conditions are correct for request metadata region.
- High latency with dedicated: verify GPU model selection & quantization flags on the variant — compute-opt flags may be forcing CPU emulation.

Optional extension exercises (time permitting)
- Add prefix caching layer: demonstrate token prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts to reduce cost and p50.
- Integrate model-quality eval pipeline: run a small eval harness that computes BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity on a golden prompt set and emits regression alerts.
- Demo private deployment: switch endpoint URL to a Private VPC control plane and show identical route config applied to on-prem pool.

Workshop artifacts included in the repo (what we hand attendees):
- bootstrap.sh (env + deps + small localserver)
- k8s/deploy.yaml (lite deploy for demo)
- examples/prompt-set.json (small 30 prompt QA + expected outputs for canary checks)
- scripts/patch-route.sh (uses API to modify route weights)

Checklist for Solutions Engineer before delivery
- Confirm demo dedicated pool has spare capacity and at least one quantized variant exists
- Pre-create route and set initial weights to avoid token limits during live demo
- Verify Console links in slide deck point to the correct org & region
- Run through a dry-run and intentionally cause fallback (e.g., reduce dedicated pool size) to rehearse explanation

Appendix — quick commands
- Create route (curl):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routes \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"name": "workshop-regional-route", "policy": {"...": "..."}}'

- Patch weights (bash):
  ./scripts/patch-route.sh --route workshop-regional-route --set "v1:0.9,v2-canary:0.1"

- Run local test (Node):
  npm run start:demo && curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/chat -d '{"input":"Hello world"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'

Feedback log (to update this doc after workshop):
- Add a short explainer of how cost estimation calc works in Console (request from last quarter)
- Provide a pre-made Confluence page for customers with capacity planning worksheet
- Add a step-by-step for private on-prem network routing (customers asked for IP whitelisting sample)

Notes to self:
- Consider creating a lightweight UI to flip weights during workshop vs running the patch script — lower friction for non-dev attendees.
- Record a 6-minute video that shows inducing fallback by shrinking dedicated pool capacity (useful for async customers).

End of doc.
